content: Semicircular lipoatrophy, also referred to as lipoatrophia semicircularis, is a medical condition observed in humans. It is colloquially known as ribbed thighs. This condition is characterized by a semicircular area of atrophy in the subcutaneous fatty tissue, predominantly located on the anterior aspect of the thighs. Importantly, the overlying skin and the underlying muscle tissue remain unaffected by this condition. This condition is most commonly observed in office workers. These bands are generally found at a height of approximately 72 centimeters from the ground, which coincides with the standard height of most office furniture. The precise etiology of semicircular lipoatrophy remains unclear. Further research is required to confirm these potential causative factors.
